Read Today's Paper Tata Motors CV posts Rs 2,138 crore Q2 profit SECTIONS Tata Motors CV posts Rs 2,138 crore Q2 profit By Shally Mohile , ET Bureau Last Updated: Oct 24, 2026, 12:38:00 AM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Tata Motors Ltd achieved a standalone net profit of ₹2,138 crore for the September quarter, reversing last year's loss. Revenue from operations rose significantly to ₹23,930 crore, up 42% from the previous year. Improved demand was driven by higher fleet utilization and industrial activity, according to managing director Girish Wagh. Consolidated profit also increased to ₹1,257 crore, aided by a drop in mark-to-market losses. Agencies Tata Motors Ltd’s commercial vehicle business reported a better-than-expected standalone net profit for the September quarter, supported by strong demand across the truck and bus segments, even as margins came under pressure from rising commodity cost. The company posted a standalone net profit, including joint venture Tata Cummins, of ₹2,138 crore for the second quarter, compared with a loss of ₹1,021 crore a year earlier. The average of analyst estimates compiled by Bloomberg was for a net profit Rs 1933.5 crore. Revenue from operations rose 42% to ₹23,930 crore. Improved fleet utilisation, stronger goods movement and higher industrial activity and mining output boosted commercial vehicle sales during the quarter, managing director and chief executive Girish Wagh said in a post-earnings media call. “Even as we expect growth in the second half of the year to moderate due to last year’s high base, the industry should end FY27 with double-digit growth and Tata Motors is likely to outperform,” he said. Live Events The company generated free cash flow of ₹4,606 crore during the quarter, taking its net cash position to ₹11,300 crore. Wagh said Tata Motors maintained margins sequentially through cost management, operational efficiencies and calibrated pricing actions, despite higher steel and rubber costs. The margin at 11.7%, however, fell 0.9 percentage points from a year earlier. The standalone results also included an exceptional gain of ₹218 crore, mainly due to the reversal of provisions under labour codes. On a consolidated basis, including contributions from subsidiaries, the company reported a net profit of ₹1,257 crore, compared with a loss of ₹867 crore a year earlier. Revenue rose more than 36% to ₹25,338 crore from ₹18,585 crore. The company attributed the improvement in consolidated profit partly to a lower mark-to-market loss on investments in Tata Capital Ltd . Its consolidated net cash position stood at ₹15,900 crore at the end of September. Total wholesale volumes rose 42% to 135,100 units during the quarter, with domestic sales increasing 30% and exports growing 177%. It had a 36.2% share in India’s commercial vehicle market in the first half of FY27, compared with 35.1% in FY26. Add as a Reliable and Trusted News Source Add Now! At 10.20 AM, Sensex dropped over 300 points to 74,460 while Nifty 50 lost nearly 100 points to trade below the 23,100 level. Broader markets also remained in the red, with Nifty Smallcap 100 and Nifty Midcap 100 indices dropping up to 0.5%. The benchmarks Nifty and Sensex had jumped nearly 3% last week, their best weekly performances in six months, aided by a rally in IT stocks after stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings and a selloff in global AI markets that prompted value-buying elsewhere. Axis Bank shares dropped around 4% to lead losses on Sensex, while HDFC Bank, Bajaj Finserv, HUL, Infosys, NTPC, Trent and Kotak Mahindra Bank shares fell around 1% each. Bucking the trend, SBI and UltraTech Cement shares gained around 2% each, while Reliance Industries, TCS, Adani Ports, Titan, HCL Tech, L&T, Power Grid and Maruti Suzuki shares gained around 1% each. Among the sectors, Nifty PSU Bank index jumped around 3% to lead gains amid a muted market. Nifty Private Bank however slipped more than 1%. For Reliance Industries, which currently owns about 66.4% of Jio Platforms, that valuation puts its stake at roughly Rs 6.8 lakh crore. The question is whether the stock market is assigning the parent company the full value of that holding. What is holding company discount? A holding company discount arises when a parent company's stock market valuation is lower than the combined estimated value of the businesses and investments it owns, after accounting for debt and other liabilities. Investors often apply such discounts because shareholders of the parent do not directly own or control its subsidiaries' assets. The discount can also reflect corporate complexity, taxes associated with selling investments, capital allocation concerns and uncertainty over when the value of subsidiaries will reach shareholders. Live Events In Reliance's case, investors are valuing a diversified group with interests spanning oil refining, petrochemicals, telecom, retail and new energy. Even if Jio commands a higher valuation after listing, that does not automatically mean RIL shares will rise by a corresponding amount. The bank said the reported figures were indicative and subject to revision as it assessed the implications of the ruling. The dispute dates back to March 2020, when Yes Bank was placed under a moratorium by the RBI following a sharp deterioration in its financial position, mounting bad loans and concerns over governance. Net interest income rose 24% to Rs 13,335 crore from Rs 10,785 crore in the year-ago quarter. Net total income increased 23% to Rs 15,974 crore from Rs 12,982 crore. Live Events Profit before tax rose 29% to Rs 8,537 crore from Rs 6,608 crore in the year-ago quarter. Excluding a prudent management and macroeconomic provision of Rs 337 crore, profit before tax grew 34% to Rs 8,874 crore. Operating expenses as a proportion of net total income stood at 33%, marginally lower than 33.1% in the year-ago quarter. Loan losses and provisions rose to Rs 2,166 crore from Rs 2,080 crore a year earlier. Excluding the additional provision of Rs 337 crore, loan losses and provisions declined 12% to Rs 1,829 crore. The annualised ratio of loan losses and provisions to average assets under finance stood at 1.56%, compared with 1.88% a year earlier. Excluding the additional provision, the ratio was 1.32%. Demand also came from all of India’s top 10 mutual funds including SBI Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund, Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund, Nippon India Mutual Fund and Kotak Mutual Fund. Insurance and pension investors include LIC , HDFC Life , SBI Life , SBI Pension, HDFC Pension and ICICI Prudential. Foreign funds pursuing long-term investments, sovereign wealth funds and pension funds accounted for the bulk of demand, according to the details. “Some long-term investors may buy additional shares in the open market after listing, given the limited allocations in the anchor book,” one source said. In that dramatic reset lies the story of Jio’s rise and the investment case behind billionaire Mukesh Ambani seeking ₹10 lakh crore valuation for Reliance’s telecom and digital play’s IPO. Jio did more than cut prices. It changed how India accesses the internet, accelerated the shift from voice to data and created an enormous digital distribution network that now carries about 60% of the country’s wireless data traffic. The company is now asking investors to value it not merely as a telecom operator, but as a broader technology platform spanning 5G, fixed broadband, cloud, entertainment, enterprise services and artificial intelligence. When Jio entered the market, industry download speeds were around 2.5 megabits per second. By FY26, speeds had risen to more than 68 Mbps, according to a Systematix report. At the same time, the cost of data fell from ₹228 per GB to ₹7.5 per GB. Average monthly data consumption rose from less than 0.2 GB per customer to 26.7 GB. The issue, which opens on Oct. 21 and closes on Oct. 23, is entirely a fresh issue with no offer-for-sale component. At the upper price band of ₹1,119, Jio Platforms will have an implied market capitalisation of about ₹10.3 lakh crore. Most of the proceeds, up to ₹27,500 crore, will be used to repay or prepay borrowings at Reliance Jio Infocomm. The offering is therefore not just a monetisation event for existing shareholders. Mumbai: Telecom equipment and optical fibre maker HFCL reported a fivefold increase in its net profit for July-September, while revenue rose nearly 2.44 times, making it the company's best quarter to date. Net profit surged 448.14% year-on-year to ₹394.22 crore from ₹71.92 crore a year ago, while revenue increased 143.62% to ₹2,541.79 crore from ₹1,043.34 crore. Sequentially, profit increased 60.49% from the previous month, and revenue rose 32.73%. "Demand continues to accelerate across AI infrastructure, hyperscale data centres and telecom networks. "Based on current expectations and business visibility, we now expect revenue growth of at least 80% in FY27 over FY26," he said. The company could reach its ₹10,000 crore annual revenue milestone ahead of its earlier target of 2028-29, he added. Live Events HFCL had announced a series of large overseas contract wins. In September, it disclosed a long-term optical fibre cable supply pact worth about $244 million (₹2,329 crore). A month earlier, it announced export orders worth about ₹522.73 crore. ET Online OYO parent PRISM is planning to nearly halve the size of the fresh issue in its proposed initial public offering (IPO) to up to Rs 3,350 crore from almost Rs 6,650 crore, sources said on Tuesday. People familiar with the matter told PTI the reduction in the issue size follows continued strong cash generation and an improving balance-sheet position, which has lowered the amount of capital the company needs to raise compared with what was originally envisaged. "The original issue was sized before the company's more recent financial performance came through. With cash generation remaining strong and the balance sheet improving, the funding requirement has come down, allowing the company to reduce the amount of primary capital it raises. "The objective is to raise what the business needs while keeping the capital structure efficient. The plan is to repay the residual debt over the next two to three years through cash flows generated by the business," a person familiar with the matter said. Earlier, OYO had planned to raise up to Rs 6,650 crore through an IPO, of which around Rs 5,000 crore was intended for debt repayment. Live Events The revised issue size comes with PRISM continuing to focus on reducing its outstanding debt. Under the revised structure, most of the issue proceeds are proposed to be used towards repayment or prepayment, in part or full, of certain borrowings. The revised issue comes as PRISM moves towards the next stage of its proposed IPO following its earlier filing of the UDRHP (Updated Draft Herring Prospectus). Moody's Ratings has revised the outlook on PRISM to 'positive' from 'stable', while reaffirming the travel tech unicorn's B2 corporate family rating. Explaining the rationale behind ratings, Moody's said, "We expect OYO's EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation) to grow to around Rs 3,000 crore (USD 315 million) over the next 12-18 months as the company continues to scale and add new storefronts to its platform. For FY26, OYO's EBITDA more than doubled to Rs 2,630 crore from Rs 1,080 crore in FY25. OYO was founded in 2013 by Ritesh Agarwal, who currently holds a 30.52 per cent stake in the company. ANI EAAA India Alternatives Ltd, an arm of Edelweiss Financial Services , will open its Rs 1,200-crore initial public offering (IPO) for subscription on October 26. The issue will close on October 28, while anchor investor bidding is scheduled for October 23, according to the company's Red Herring Prospectus (RHP). The issue is entirely an Offer for Sale (OFS) by Edelweiss Group with no fresh issue component. This means the company will not receive any proceeds from the public offering, and the entire amount will go to the selling shareholder. The IPO size has been reduced to Rs 1,200 crore from the Rs 1,500 crore proposed in the Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) filed with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) in January. In March, Edelweiss Financial Services completed the sale of 4.4 per cent of common equity in its arm EAAA India Alternatives for Rs 375 crore. Live Events Incorporated in 2008, EAAA India Alternatives is among India's leading alternative investment platforms, with over 15 years of experience in managing long-term capital. The company operates a diversified, multi-strategy platform across alternative asset classes, focusing on income and yield solutions for clients. Its investment portfolio spans real assets, including infrastructure assets in the energy and transportation sectors, commercial real estate, and private credit, which offers financing solutions across the risk spectrum. The company has offices in Mumbai, New Delhi, GIFT City and Singapore. Also, SEC Environmental Technologies Ltd is gearing up to launch its IPO on October 27. The IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 150 crore and an Offer for Sale (OFS) of up to 1,56,82,750 equity shares, according to the Red Herring Prospectus. Where should investors bet as Ambani's Rs 30,213 crore issue opens By Akash Podishetti , ETMarkets.com Last Updated: Oct 21, 2026, 09:48:00 AM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Jio Platforms is eyeing a staggering valuation of Rs 10 lakh crore for its upcoming IPO, sparking heated debates among analysts on whether to pursue Jio or Reliance Industries shares. The IPO holds the potential for investors to capitalize on India's booming digital economy, focusing specifically on Jio's telecommunications prowess, while Reliance offers broader sector diversification. ETMarkets.com With Jio Platforms seeking a Rs 10 lakh crore valuation in its IPO , analysts are divided over whether investors would be better off subscribing to the issue or buying shares of parent Reliance Industries . While some see greater value in RIL , given the discount on its Jio holding and its other businesses, others favour the telecom company for direct exposure to India's growing digital economy. At the upper end of its IPO price band of Rs 1,119, Jio Platforms is valued at Rs 10.3 lakh crore. Reliance Industries, which holds 66.43% of Jio before the offering, is expected to retain about 64.5% after the issue, giving its stake a market value of Rs 6.64 lakh crore. For Jio IPO LIVE updates, click here The numbers have brought renewed attention to the valuation of Reliance Industries and whether investors could get Jio exposure at a more attractive price by buying shares of its parent company. Arpit Jain, Joint MD at Arihant Capital Markets , said that applying a standard 30% holding-company discount to Reliance's stake in Jio brings its attributable value down to about Rs 4.65 lakh crore. This means investors buying RIL shares are also gaining exposure to businesses such as Reliance Retail, oil-to-chemicals (O2C), new energy and media, which Jain believes could offer attractive value at current valuations. Live Events Reliance Retail generates annual EBITDA of around Rs 27,000 crore, while the O2C business contributes about Rs 80,000 crore. Its investments in renewable energy, green hydrogen and media could offer further long-term growth opportunities. "Reliance Industries may appeal to investors seeking a diversified investment with potential value-unlocking opportunities across businesses, while Jio Platforms may be more suitable for those looking for focused exposure to India's digital and technology growth story," Jain said. Why investors may prefer Jio IPO For investors looking to participate directly in India's telecom and digital services growth, Jio offers a more focused investment opportunity. The company has more than 53 crore subscribers and has emerged as the country's largest telecom operator. Its growth prospects are supported by rising data consumption, improving average revenue per user (ARPU), expanding home broadband penetration and opportunities in enterprise services and artificial intelligence. Chemical stocks led losses, while banking shares remained under pressure following disappointing results from private-sector lenders earlier in the week. Market breadth on the NSE remained negative, with 2,988 stocks advancing against 608 declining, while 102 stocks were unchanged, out of a total of 3,698 stocks traded. Zerodha Fund House has launched the Zerodha BSE Top 10 Banks ETF , an open-ended exchange-traded fund (ETF) that seeks to track the performance of the BSE Top 10 Banks Index , offering investors exposure to India's 10 largest banks through a single investment. The new fund offer (NFO) opened on October 12, 2026, and will close on October 26, 2026. Investors can subscribe to the NFO with a minimum investment of Rs 1,000 and in multiples of Rs 1,000 thereafter. The BSE Top 10 Banks Index comprises the largest banks in the BSE 500, selected on the basis of free-float market capitalisation. The index includes both private and public sector banks, with constituent weights reflecting their relative size, subject to applicable limits. According to Zerodha Fund House, India has 41 listed banks, and the 10 banks represented in the index account for approximately 89% of the free-float market value of the banking sector. The ETF allows investors to gain exposure to this basket without having to purchase each bank's shares individually. Banking sector's role in economic growth Live Events Banks play a key role in financing India's economic activity by providing credit to businesses and individuals. According to the fund house, bank lending to sectors such as agriculture and allied activities, industry, services and personal loans has grown year on year in recent years. The ETF is designed for investors who want to take a focused exposure to the banking sector as part of their investment portfolio. Since the scheme tracks a sector-specific index, its performance will depend on the performance of the underlying banking stocks and the broader banking industry. The fund house also noted that several major banks in the index are trading below their respective five-year average price-to-book value ratios. The price-to-book ratio compares a bank's market valuation with its book value, making it one of the metrics investors use to assess banking stocks. However, a valuation below the historical average does not necessarily mean a stock is undervalued or that its price will rise. Agencies The Indian rupee strengthened sharply on Wednesday, helped along by foreign portfolio inflows linked to Jio Platforms' IPO while persistently elevated oil prices kept traders cautious about positioning for further gains in the unit. The rupee closed up 0.5% at 94.46 against the dollar after touching a peak of 94.43 earlier in the day, its strongest level since early September. It trimmed gains in the latter half of the session as oil prices rose and local stocks fell. Brent crude oil futures were last up 1.3% at over $110 per barrel while India's benchmark equity index, the Nifty 50, declined 0.7%. Escalating Middle East tensions fuelled fears of supply disruptions, lifting oil prices after Iran told Pakistan's army chief there would be no talks with Washington until its demands were met. "Volatility in oil will keep rupee a little on the defensive but sharp falls are unlikely in the near term," a trader at a state-run lender said. Live Events Despite the global headwinds, inflows linked to Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion IPO aided the rupee. The IPO was fully subscribed in less than two hours of public bidding on Wednesday as investors flocked to India's largest share sale. "With USD/INR holding below 95.00, focus shifts to 94.80-94.70. A sustained break below 94.80 could open the way towards 94.00 over the coming weeks, keeping the near-term outlook favourable for the rupee," said Amit Pabari, managing director at FX advisory firm CR Forex. Elsewhere, Asian currencies were mostly rangebound and the dollar index was little changed at 101.8. Focus will now turn to the release of the minutes of the RBI's latest monetary policy review held earlier this month. The central bank had delivered its first rate hike in four years on October 7 and signalled more were likely to come. Data released last week showed that India's retail inflation accelerated to a higher-than-expected 5.54% in September. Agencies The Indian rupee snapped an eight-session-long winning streak on Thursday as Brent oil prices climbed to their highest since May on deepening worries about conflict in the Middle East, which hammered global equities as well. The South Asian currency endured a volatile trading session, swinging from its strongest level in over six weeks to close down 0.4% at 94.8175 per dollar. Earlier in the day, chunky foreign inflows for Jio Platforms' IPO added to tailwinds from the Reserve Bank of India 's defensive measures that had boosted the currency but its gains faded as oil prices climbed in the latter half. Traders pointed to broad-based dollar demand locally alongside broader signs of a risk-off move in global markets. MSCI's All-World index was set for its largest daily fall in two weeks, down 0.4%, as tech shares from Seoul and Tokyo to Amsterdam and Paris came under pressure. Equity futures pointed to a weak start for shares on Wall Street as well. Live Events OIL PRICES REMAIN A KEY RISK Oil prices have remained elevated despite oil flows from the Gulf holding up, reflecting market anxieties over the conflict. "The sizeable risk premium currently embedded in prices is unlikely to fade until clear signs of de-escalation emerge and reassure investors that regional supply will remain uninterrupted," ING said in a note. Brent oil prices were last up 3.3% at $112.40 per barrel. India imports nearly 90% of its crude requirements, making it one of the world's most vulnerable economies to the Middle East oil shock . This remains a key risk for the rupee, with market participants and observers split over how sternly the RBI should defend the currency in the face of fundamental pressures. While senior IMF official Krishna Srinivasan said on Wednesday that India should allow the dollar-rupee exchange rate to move as the first line of defence, former RBI deputy governor Michael Debabrata Patra told Reuters that exchange rates tend to overshoot and can cause financial stability risks. When a WhatsApp group is suspended or banned, its members may receive fresh invitations from a different mobile number asking them to join another group. Sebi said investors should treat such invitations as warning signs and leave these groups rather than follow operators to new ones. The regulator advised investors to avoid invitation-only WhatsApp groups run by unknown individuals or people claiming to be stock market experts, particularly when the groups are operated through overseas numbers. It also cautioned investors against relying on messages posted by other group members claiming to have earned profits or successfully executed trades based on the recommendations. According to Sebi, these testimonials and trade confirmations could be planted by individuals working with the operators. Nevertheless, analysts maintain that there are glimmers of hope for the upcoming week; a rally among large-cap stocks could pave the way for investor opportunities. ETMarkets.com The Indian stock market extended losses despite positive tailwinds on Friday morning, with Sensex and Nifty falling up to half a percent as oil prices soared higher. Sensex fell over 400 points to drop to 72,844 while Nifty 50 lost over 200 points to trade below the 22,500 level, as seen at around 10.20 AM. Broader markets crashed deeper into the red, with Nifty Smallcap 100 and Nifty Midcap 100 indices falling up to 3%. Sensex had opened in the green, led by gains in IT stocks amid a rout in global AI-linked stocks, but eventually plunged into the red, erasing the 500-pt morning gains. Among the sectors, Nifty Metal and Nifty Consumer Durables plunged around 3% while Nifty Auto, Nifty PSU Bank, Nifty Realty and several others dropped around 2% each. Nifty IT however jumped 1%. The overall market breadth remained sharply negative, with NSE seeing 407 advances against 2,778 declines, while 102 stocks remained unchanged. What lies ahead for Dalal Street? Brent crude spiking to $114 is a major negative for the economy and markets, said V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments. However, there are strong positives that can counter this negative, he said. “The sharp decline in the US 10-year yield to 4.96 % and the appreciation in the rupee to 94.70 to the dollar are positives that can restrain FII selling significantly. More importantly, more than Rs 3 lakh of the IPO money will come back into the system after the allotment is completed by next Monday. This potential liquidity surge can lift the market next week. The market can move higher anticipating this in advance,” the analyst said. Live Events It is important to understand that the rally, if it happens, will be led by the large-caps which are signalling resilience, Vijayakumar said. The sharp correction in the broader market, particularly in small-caps, might continue since their valuations, driven up by liquidity rather than fundamentals, are hard to justify. Fairly-valued large-caps, particularly those which are growing well, present value buying opportunities for patient investors, according to the analyst. The bank's net interest income increased by 4% year-on-year to Rs 4,569 crore, driven by enhanced asset quality, while gross non-performing assets decreased to 2.73% of gross advances, indicating robust profitability and growth momentum. ETMarkets.com IndusInd Bank on Friday reported a standalone net profit of Rs 1176 crore in the second quarter as against a loss of Rs 445 crore in the same quarter of last year. Net interest income rose 4% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 4,569 crore. On a consolidated basis, the company reported a net profit of Rs 1,242 crore for the September quarter. The decline in bad loans and lower provisioning requirements supported the bank's recovery in profitability. Provisions and contingencies, excluding tax, declined 54% to Rs 1,223 crore from Rs 2,631 crore in the year-ago quarter. Fee and other income jumped 36% YoY to Rs 2,248 crore from Rs 1,651 crore, while net revenue increased 12.5% to Rs 6,817 crore from Rs 6,060 crore. Pre-provision operating profit (PPOP), a key measure of a bank's operating performance, surged 40% to Rs 2,874 crore compared with Rs 2,047 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Live Events Operating expenses declined to Rs 3,943 crore from Rs 4,013 crore. The bank's yield on assets stood at 8.35%, compared with 8.75% a year earlier, while its cost of funds declined to 5.11% from 5.43%. Asset quality IndusInd Bank reported an improvement in asset quality during the quarter, with gross non-performing assets (GNPA) declining to 2.73% of gross advances from 3.25% in the June quarter and 3.6% a year earlier. Net NPA declined to 0.83% from 0.95% in the preceding quarter and 1.04% in the corresponding period last year. The provision coverage ratio stood at 70.19% at the end of September, compared with 71.81% a year earlier. Commenting on the results, Rajiv Anand, md and CEO of IndusInd Bank, said the September quarter reflected improving business momentum and profitability. Following a brief uptick at the start of trading, the rupee ended lower against the US dollar. Brent crude prices have surged to a five-month peak, raising worries about energy supply interruptions. This led to a pullback from technology stocks as investors flocked towards safer investments like US Treasuries. Agencies The Indian rupee weakened for a second straight session on Friday as surging oil prices spurred risk aversion, erasing gains made earlier in the week and leaving the currency little changed, despite easing expectations of further US rate hikes. The rupee opened the session marginally higher at 94.79 against the US dollar , but turned lower in early trades to hit a low of 94.9725. The currency ended 0.1% lower for the day at 94.9400, after depreciating by 0.4% on Thursday. It was little changed for the week, after rising 1.4% last week. Oil prices rose in the latter half of the week including in Asian hours, with the benchmark Brent crude touching a more than five-month high, after attacks in Saudi Arabia by Yemen's Houthis stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies from the region. The Brent crude contract was hovering around $114 per barrel, and is on track to post a third straight weekly surge. While facing a shock from oil prices, investors have been reassessing technology trades and pulling back from riskier assets on worries about stretched valuations for artificial intelligence-led companies, leading to a selloff in stocks and rising demand for safe-haven US Treasuries. Live Events The odds of a rate hike by the Federal Reserve have dropped to single digits from as high as 70% a month ago, which provided brief relief to the rupee in the early session, but oil worries outweighed the positive move. Energy prices have remained elevated fuelling concerns about inflation and imported energy costs, which hit the nation's current account calculations. Currency traders also cited some residual flows linked to the Jio Platforms initial public offering. These flows, alongside the unwinding of dollar-long positions triggered by the Reserve Bank of India 's latest measures, had lifted the currency to a six-week high of 94.30 per dollar on Thursday, before importers stepped up dollar purchases. "The RBI's recent FX measures are short-term stabilizers, not necessarily unjustified, but insufficient to alter the medium-term bearish outlook on the rupee," Apoorva Javadekar, chief economist at Shriram Research, said. Prominent institutional investors and major domestic mutual fund houses participated in the anchor allocation. IANS IPO listing at Nasdaq. EAAA India Alternatives has raised around Rs 360 crore from anchor investors ahead of its initial public offering (IPO), which opens for public subscription on October 26. The alternative investment management platform informed the stock exchanges that it had allotted 21,62,161 equity shares to anchor investors at Rs 1,665 apiece, the upper end of the IPO price band. The anchor book saw participation from marquee global institutional investors, including Norway’s Government Pension Fund Global, one of the world’s largest sovereign wealth funds managed by Norges Bank Investment Management, and global asset manager Schroders. Other long-only foreign institutional investors also participated in the placement. Domestic mutual funds accounted for a significant share of the anchor allocation, with all five of India’s largest mutual fund houses — HDFC Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, SBI Mutual Fund, Nippon India Mutual Fund and Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund — participating in the book. In all, 10 mutual funds invested in the anchor round, accounting for 61% of the total allocation. Other participating fund houses included Bandhan Mutual Fund, HSBC Mutual Fund, 360 ONE Mutual Fund, Abakkus Mutual Fund and Trust Mutual Fund. Indian asset managers such as Carnelian, 360 ONE, Unifi and Nuvama also participated in the anchor placement. IPO details The Rs 1,200-crore IPO of EAAA India Alternatives is entirely an offer for sale (OFS), through which promoter Edelweiss Securities and Investments Private Limited will divest 72.07 lakh shares. The company will not receive any proceeds from the issue, with the proceeds accruing to the selling promoter. The IPO has a price band of Rs 1,585-1,665 per share and will remain open for subscription from October 26 to October 28. Live Events The minimum application size for retail investors is nine shares, translating into an investment of Rs 14,985 at the upper end of the price band. The allotment is expected to be finalised on October 29, while the shares are tentatively scheduled to list on the BSE and NSE on November 2. Axis Capital , Jefferies, Motilal Oswal and Nuvama are the book-running lead managers to the issue. Higher steel production and sales boosted earnings, while adjusted EBITDA grew 33% and net debt declined sequentially. " src="https://img.etimg.com/thumb/msid-135149786,width-210,height-158,imgsize-108320,resizemode-75/jindal-steel-q2-profit-rises-21-as-revenue-hits-record-rs-19448-crorebr.jpg"> Agencies Jindal Steel posts record quarterly revenue as profits, steel production and sales increase, EBITDA improves, and net debt declines, despite a fall in share price. Jindal Steel ’s consolidated profit increased 21% year-on-year to Rs 771 crore in July-September, anchored by a 44% year-on-year surge in gross revenue to an all-time high of Rs 19,448 crore. Both revenue and profit surpassed analysts’ estimates during the second quarter of this financial year. The company reported its earnings during market hours on Friday, and its shares closed at Rs 1,012.00 apiece on the BSE, down 1.7% from the previous close. Consolidated steel production increased to 2.4 million tonnes during the quarter, up from 2 million tonnes a year ago, while sales rose to 2.38 million tonnes from 1.87 million tonnes. Adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) increased 33% year-on-year to Rs 2,504 crore in July-September, while adjusted Ebitda on each tonne of steel stood at Rs 10,529 per tonne during the quarter, up from Rs 10,010 per tonne a year ago. The company sold a higher share of flat products in its overall sales mix and fewer thermo-mechanically treated rebars among its long products, boosting the average selling price, according to its statement. Live Events Jindal Steel’s consolidated net debt fell to Rs 14,786 crore at the end of September from Rs 15,927 crore at the end of the June quarter. Its net debt-to-Ebitda ratio stood at 1.51 times, down from 1.71 times a quarter ago. The company incurred capital expenditure of Rs 1,228 crore during the quarter. State-owned Maharatna company Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL) on Friday reported a 21.45% year-on-year (YoY) decline in profit attributable to owners at Rs 4,863.05 crore in Q2FY27 from Rs 6,191.49 crore in Q2FY26. However, on a sequential basis, the company posted a strong turnaround in the September quarter, against a loss of Rs 3,962.13 crore in the previous quarter (Q1FY27). The company's revenue from operations gained 29.78% YoY at Rs 1,57,817.93 crore in the quarter under review, compared with Rs 1,21,604.70 crore reported in Q2FY26. Total expenses at the state-owned company rose 32.54% YoY to Rs 1,51,932.8 crore against Rs 1,14,634.91 crore in the year-ago quarter. On a sequential basis, earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) stood at Rs 8,971 crore, compared with a loss of Rs 4,077 crore in the preceding quarter. EBITDA margin came in at 6.02%. Separately, BPCL's board of directors, at a meeting held on October 23, approved the incorporation of a wholly owned subsidiary in India for the proposed greenfield refinery and petrochemical complex and associated facilities at Ramayapatnam in Andhra Pradesh. The incorporation is subject to requisite government, statutory and regulatory approvals. The subsidiary will serve as a dedicated project company, with an initial authorised share capital of up to Rs 4,900 crore. Live Events According to the company, the entity will provide a dedicated legal and governance structure for project activities and support due diligence, engagement with lenders and potential partners, and the development of an optimal financing and partnership structure. The detailed feasibility reports are being finalised. The financial investment decision and financial commitments will be considered separately by the competent authorities at the appropriate stage, BPCL said. BPCL shares ended Friday's session on the NSE at Rs 281.95, down 1.74% from the previous close of Rs 286.95. The stock traded in a range of Rs 277.05-Rs 286.40 during the session.
